item.title: Marine Le Pen's National Rally plans to "sanction" the wearing of the veil with a fine
item.description: The National Rally plans to "penalize the wearing of the Islamic veil" with "a fine" if it comes to power, MP Jean-Philippe Tanguy, Marine Le Pen's lieutenant in the presidential election, stated on Sunday. item.title: Former French PM Édouard Balladur, once defeated by ally Jacques Chirac, dies at 97
item.description: Édouard Balladur, who served as prime minister of France from 1993 to 1995, died on Monday at the age of 97. He led a "cohabitation" government under Socialist president François Mitterrand before waging a bitter battle for the presidency against his friend Jacques Chirac in 1995 – a race he ultimately lost. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: US President Donald Trump will meet oil refining executives on Tuesday as he tries to tame fuel prices sent spiralling by the Iran war ahead of midterm elections in November, the White House said. item.title: ‘Uncertainties’ rising: Xi calls for stronger cooperation in meeting with Putin
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping met at the SCO summit. They discussed strengthening bilateral ties and international regional issues. Cooperation in artificial intelligence and digital innovation was also a key topic. Russia proposed making the bilateral visa-free regime permanent for Chinese citizens. The leaders also touched upon the Ukraine conflict during their talks. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: As Icelanders say no to resuming EU talks, what issues weighed in the election?
item.description: Iceland's voters rejected restarting negotiations to join the European Union in a referendum that pitted concerns about geopolitical stability against keeping national control of Iceland’s prized fisheries. Talks with the EU to join the bloc had begun after the 2008 financial crisis but had been ended by a Eurosceptic government. But why did Icelanders say no? FRANCE 24's Armen Georgian tells us more. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: With no clear contender, "everyone thinks they have a shot"' at succeeding to Macron
item.description: There are eight months left until the next french Presidential election, politicians are ramping up their campaigning, with interviews, meetings and public statements. As it gets closer, more and more candidates are vying for a spot on the starting line. For now, far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is topping the polls - what is unknown is who she will be facing in the second round. FRANCE 24's Marc Perelman tells us more. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France's politicians look to close gap with far right ahead of key election
item.description: With eight months until the next french Presidential election, politicians are ramping up their campaigning, with interviews, meetings and public statements. But who exactly will run has yet to be decided. The centre-left socialists and Place Publique parties will hold a primary in October to elect one candidate, as to not dilute the vote. While centrist and centre-right candidates are also having to decide between rivalry and unity. The dilemma? How to best stave off the rise of the far right and left. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: ¿Cómo ha cambiado la situación en Gaza a casi tres años del inicio de los ataques israelíes?
item.description: A semanas de las elecciones en Israel, los ataques contra la Franja de Gaza no dan tregua a pesar del acuerdo pactado con Hamás con la mediación de Estados Unidos. Según cifras del Ministerio de Salud palestino, respaldadas por la ONU, al menos 73.000 personas han muerto hasta mediados de 2026 en el enclave por los ataques israelíes. En el Invitado del Día de France 24 analizamos la situación en Gaza a casi tres años del inicio de los ataques por parte de Tel Aviv con Xavier Abu Eid, politólogo y magister en diplomacia. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: ¿Qué responde el Gobierno colombiano tras el bombardeo contra disidencias de las FARC en el que murieron tres menores?
item.description: El Gobierno colombiano defendió este lunes 31 de agosto el bombardeo ejecutado contra una estructura disidente de las FARC en el departamento del Guaviare, en el que murieron diez combatientes, entre ellos tres menores de edad: dos de 15 años y uno de 16. El Ministerio de Defensa aseguró que la operación, ordenada por el presidente Abelardo de la Espriella y realizada el pasado 27 de agosto, cumplió los estándares legales para este tipo de ataques. Las autoridades atribuyeron la presencia de los menores en el campamento al reclutamiento forzado y utilización de niños y adolescentes por parte… Fuente: France 24 - Español.
